A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T* framework and LV-HAYSTACK benchmark. All 22 pages, including Appendices A–H, are readable, and the text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original search-utility, efficiency, downstream QA, ablation, and correlation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results, including the search evaluations, downstream QA experiments, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Appendix D retain the same question grounding, iterative grid search, scoring updates, keyframe selection, and trainable objective. Shortening Table 5's label from 'Detector-based T*' to 'T*' does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Coverage remains LV-HAYSTACK's egocentric and allocentric subsets, LongVideoBench, Video-MME, NExT-QA, EgoSchema, and Ego4D LongVideo QA, including the same clip-level and full-video scenarios.

E2.justification: The comparator rows in Tables 2–6 and the appendix comparisons are unchanged. Table 5 adds citation [28] to the existing eight-frame LLaVA-OneVision-7B row without adding a comparison method.

E3.justification: The reported splits, frame budgets, model configurations, five-second temporal threshold, subtitle exclusions, preprocessing, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendices D–E.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same grounding-resource, grid-size, threshold, semantic-metric, correlation, search-complexity, and qualitative analyses. Enlarging Figure 3 redisplays the existing sampling-dynamics analysis.

E5.justification: Table 10 already reports means and standard deviations over two T* runs in v1 and retains that practice in v3. Table 9's Pearson/Spearman correlations and p-value reporting are also unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 4 reports the same 32-frame LongVideoBench XLong accuracies for GPT-4o + T* (53.1%) and LLaVA-OneVision-72B + T* (62.4%) in both versions.

T1.justification: The task definitions, similarity and precision/recall formulations, search equations, Appendix B complexity derivations, and Appendix D training-objective equations are retained without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution, temporal-search-as-spatial-search proposal, and claims about search efficiency and downstream QA benefits. The title prefix does not change these claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of efficiency, sampling dynamics, video-length effects, and search utility remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning sparse-keyframe assumptions, dense reasoning, and exclusion of audio and subtitles.

D1.justification: The embedded Live Demo link gains a /demo path, and the Video link changes host. Table 5 also drops its detector-specific qualifier. Appendix implementation details, hardware, annotation instructions, prompts, and code/data links are retained. The PDFs do not establish whether the revised destinations improve availability.

R1.justification: Section 7 changes the characterization of LVBench [65] and MLVU [93] from evaluating 'only' downstream QA to 'mostly' downstream QA, modestly qualifying the positioning against prior benchmarks. The cited-work set is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds 'T*:' to the title, makes limited wording and labeling edits, and removes the funding and code-assistance acknowledgments. The section organization and appendix narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 enlarges Figure 3 and increases spacing between Figure 1's caption and the Introduction heading, with associated text reflow. Figures and tables retain their underlying content and structure; there is no substantial visual reorganization.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a small readability gain through the enlarged Figure 3 and clearer separation of Figure 1's caption from the Introduction. Its related-work wording is also less categorical. Scientific support remains unchanged, while removing acknowledgments and Table 5's detector-specific label loses some attribution and specificity, limiting the overall benefit.
